title: Custom validation rules
idea: A validator is a list of express-validator rules plus one `validate` middleware. It stops a bad body with a `422` that names every failing field.

analogy.text: A customs officer ticks each field on a form, then either stamps it through or sends it back with every problem marked.
analogy.breaks: Rules only record problems. `validate` is the one that replies.

points: `body('email')` starts a chain for one field; each method adds a rule.
`withMessage` names the rule before it; `bail()` stops the chain after a failure.
`custom` runs your function; a falsy result or a throw fails the rule.
In the route, put the rules array first and `validate` right after it.

hero.title: A body through rules and validate

steps.caption: The body enters the chains. Each rule reads one field of `req.body`; `trim` also rewrites it.
A failing rule adds an error to the request. Nothing is sent yet.
`validate` asks `validationResult` for the recorded errors. With none, it calls `next()`.
With errors, it throws `ApiError(422)` holding one `{ field, message }` per failing field.

code.title: Rules and validate
code.caption: Each commented block is a project file, cut down. A stand-in controller replies, so no database is needed. Press Run.

walk.text: A custom rule takes `(value, { req })`. `false` or a throw fails it; `req` reaches other fields.
A chain: `trim` cleans, `notEmpty` and `isEmail` check, `withMessage` names each failure.
`bail()` stops the chain at a failure, so a field reports one message.
`isString` guards the string methods after it. `custom` plugs in your function and its message.
`validate` reads the recorded errors. If any exist, it throws `ApiError(422)`.
Rules run in order: the rules array, then `validate`, then the controller.
Five bodies: three break rules, one sends an object, one is valid but padded with spaces.

pitfalls: Without `bail()`, an empty email reports both "required" and "invalid".
A `custom` rule that throws reports its own message; add `withMessage` to keep internals private.
Never send `errors.array()` as is: each error holds the submitted `value`, even a password.

quiz.why: Every rule in a chain runs, even after a failure. Without `bail()`, an empty email fails both `notEmpty` and `isEmail`.

takeaway: One `validate` middleware gives every route the same `422` shape.

starters: Why use `422` and not `400` for invalid data?
How do I write a rule that checks the database?
Why does `trim` change `req.body` instead of only checking it?
